findings.title: Color-shape and font-flag migrations run once per account, so any profile not active at the 1.3.0 upgrade keeps its old shape
findings.evidence: migrations[3]/[4] (MigrateColorShape, MigrateFontFlags) are gated by the account-level db.global.schemaVersion but walk only db.profile. OnProfileChanged re-runs only FoldLegacyUnits, BackfillLabelStyle, MigrateSpecKeys and BuildSpells. A scratch repro under the kit mock, after a swap to a profile at v5, gave '[1]=0.1 r=1' and fontFlags=NONE: nothing was converted. Result: customised colors read back as defaults, and the outline dropdown opens blank. The mock AceDB has no SetProfile, so no test covers this path.
findings.remediation: C-01: call MigrateColorShape and MigrateFontFlags from Database:Init and every OnProfileChanged, after MigrateSpecKeys. Both are idempotent. Keep the version steps so schemaVersion still advances. Add an `if not (db and db.profile) then return end` guard in MigrateColorShape. Mitigation: convert only when the keyed part equals the declared default, otherwise drop the array part; state this in docs/schema.md. Add a real SetProfile to tests/wow_mock.lua and a two-profile test with a 'red under' line (test_color_shape or test_database). Update the savedvariables-§1 register row in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md to name all five shape-driven steps (see KICKCD-A-08 / B-03). No schemaVersion bump.
findings.verify_reason: core/Database.lua:716-721: migrations[3] and [4] (MigrateColorShape, MigrateFontFlags) are gated on the account-level db.global.schemaVersion but only walk db.profile. MigrateProfile (lines 734-767) is a no-op once the account is at 5. Database:Init (854-906) and OnProfileChanged (805-829) re-run FoldLegacyUnits, BackfillLabelStyle, MigrateSpecKeys and BuildSpells, and nothing else. Init's own comment (lines 885-889) states this exact per-account vs per-profile trap for spell keys and fixes it only for MigrateSpecKeys. Any other profile keeps the hybrid array+keyed colors, which read back as the defaults, and keeps "NONE" font flags, which leave the outline dropdown blank. The remediation is sound: both steps are idempotent, and the keyed-vs-default guard stops stale array values from overwriting colors a user edited after the upgrade. walk() already tolerates a nil profile, so the extra guard only protects against a nil db. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:390 is the register row to update. I kept the severity because this is silent loss of saved customisation for every multi-profile user who upgraded.

findings.title: The Spells page HookScripts AceGUI's pooled Label and Dropdown frames, so its tooltips and mouse capture leak into every AceGUI consumer
findings.evidence: label.frame:EnableMouse(true) plus HookScript OnEnter/OnLeave, and dd.frame:HookScript('OnEnter', ...) showing the 'Category for future filtering…' tooltip. AceGUI recycles these frames through one process-global pool, a hook cannot be removed, and the Label and Dropdown OnAcquire reset neither scripts nor EnableMouse. Recycled labels in other addons' panels (AbsorbTracker, AuraMaster, BankLedger, ConsumableMaster, LootHistory, PanelMaster, PrettyChat) then show a KickCD spell tooltip and swallow clicks. One more hook pair is added per row per render, and F-008 doubles the renders. No test covers this.
findings.remediation: Replace the Label with AceGUI:Create('InteractiveLabel') and use SetCallback('OnEnter'/'OnLeave'). Call SetHighlight(nil) if the highlight is unwanted. Replace the dd.frame HookScript with H.AttachTooltip(dd, L['Category'], L['Category for future filtering. Currently informational only.']). This also fixes the dropdown tooltip, which never fires today because dd.frame is not mouse-enabled. Test: render twice, release, acquire a plain Label, and assert it has no OnEnter script and IsMouseEnabled() is false. Also assert the dropdown's OnEnter callback shows the tooltip. Drop the options-ui-§1 rule_ref, or cite AP #76 by analogy (AceGUI objects are process-global).
findings.verify_reason: settings/Spells.lua:662-666 is real. label.frame:EnableMouse(true) plus HookScript OnEnter/OnLeave on a pooled AceGUI Label, and the Label OnAcquire (libs/AceGUI-3.0/widgets/AceGUIWidget-Label.lua:72) resets neither the scripts nor mouse enabling. The AceGUI pool is process-global, so a recycled Label in another addon shows a stale KickCD spell tooltip and catches mouse input. The dropdown evidence is wrong, though. AceGUIWidget-DropDown.lua:647 creates the outer .frame as a plain Frame that is never mouse-enabled; mouse input goes to the child button and button_cover (lines 699 and 708). The dd.frame HookScript at Spells.lua:763-770 therefore never fires. Its tooltip is dead in KickCD today, and the cross-addon leak there is only latent. The impact is a cosmetic tooltip and hover glitch in other addons' panels, with no data or taint consequence, so the severity drops to medium. options-ui-§1 says nothing about hooking pooled frames; the closest standards anchor is the process-global-AceGUI reasoning of AP #76, applied here by analogy. The fix is correct: InteractiveLabel with SetCallback, and O.AttachTooltip (OptionsWidgets.lua:1094, which uses SetCallback on AceGUI widgets) for the dropdown. Release clears both.

findings.title: Per-unit cast-event frames are rebuilt on every enable, leaking 36 frames per disable/enable cycle
findings.locations: core/Util.lua:437-445, modules/IconGrid.lua:810-822, modules/IconGrid.lua:831-832, modules/IconGrid.lua:860-861, modules/Castbar.lua:1016-1031, modules/Castbar.lua:1044-1045, modules/Castbar.lua:1109-1110, modules/Castbar.lua:1136
findings.evidence: Util.RegisterUnitCastEvent calls CreateFrame('Frame') per event: IconGrid makes 8 per unit and Castbar 10. DisableUnit and Suspend drop them with inst.eventFrames = {}. Scratch measurement: 142 -> 178 -> 214 -> 250 frames, +36 per cycle. Reached through /kcd disable+enable, the per-unit Enable toggles, a profile switch that flips enabled, and each /kcd perf suspend/resume. The helper also accepts any eventName, which is the shape of the forbidden 'general-purpose private-frame factory'. test_disabled counts registrations by name only, so it cannot see orphaned frames.
findings.remediation: Review C-03 / audit D1: hold one filter frame per (module, unit) on inst (Util.UnitCastFilter or Util.NewUnitFilter with Arm/Disarm), created once. Re-register events on EnableUnit/Resume and UnregisterAllEvents on teardown. Use a file-scope route map so enable allocates nothing (AP #43). Change the Resume guard at Castbar.lua:1136 to an armed flag. Narrow the helper to the cast family, or document its one job. Route the RegisterUnitEvent calls through the pcall-isolated helper (A-03). Test: CreateFrame count across two disable/enable cycles adds 0; it must be red on HEAD. Add a test_util idempotency case for Arm/Disarm. Update the per-unit frames paragraph in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
findings.verify_reason: core/Util.lua:437-445 calls CreateFrame per event on every call. IconGrid.lua:810-822 registers 8 events per unit and Castbar.lua:1016-1031 registers 10. DisableUnit and Suspend (IconGrid.lua:831-832 and 860-861, Castbar.lua:1044-1045 and 1109-1110) unregister the frames and then drop them with eventFrames = {}. Castbar Resume (1136) keys the rebuild on #eventFrames == 0. Each cycle therefore orphans 18 frames per unit. events-frames-taint.md:22 says the filter frame MUST be re-used across a disable/enable cycle rather than rebuilt. slash-commands §7 (line 186) says the frame is unregistered and kept. Line 24 forbids a general-purpose private-frame factory, and RegisterUnitCastEvent takes any eventName. One caveat on the remediation: line 24 also bars a frame that picks up another event after it is created. The per-(module, unit) frame should register its fixed cast-family set, and later re-registration must only re-arm that same set.

findings.title: scheduleTimer returns nil (C_Timer.After), so the LibKa0s color-picker and slider throttle never engages

The library uses the return value as its armed flag (libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:1471-1482), so every ~60 Hz drag tick schedules its own SetAndRefresh and CONFIG_CHANGED fan-out. findings.title: An IconGrid rebuild repaints every icon 'ready' and relies on unordered CallbackHandler dispatch for correction
findings.evidence: BuildActiveList applies { ready = true, start = 0, duration = 0 } to every icon. Cooldowns and IconGrid both handle PEW, SPELLS_CHANGED, TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED, PROFILE_CHANGED and CONFIG_CHANGED, and dispatch runs in pairs order. If Cooldowns fires first, its SPELL_STATE lands on the old pool. An interrupt on cooldown can then show ready after a talent swap, pet summon, spec or profile switch, or /reload, until the next SPELL_UPDATE_*. Unverified in the client.
findings.remediation: C-06: publish a read-only Cooldowns:StateFor(spellID) returning watched[id]. After BuildActiveList, seed with btn:Apply(st or READY_SEED, true), where READY_SEED is a file-scope constant. Alternative: Cooldowns re-emits on GRID_LAYOUT. Test: register Cooldowns before IconGrid, fire PEW, and assert an on-cooldown icon is not ready. Serialize after R-03 (both touch IconGrid.lua). Smoke test C-06.
findings.verify_reason: IconGrid.lua:351 seeds every rebuilt icon with { ready = true } and force=true. IconGrid (IconGrid.lua:934-941) and Cooldowns (Cooldowns.lua:547-555) both register PEW, spec change, SPELLS_CHANGED and TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED on AceEvent's shared CallbackHandler, which dispatches in pairs order. If Cooldowns:Rebuild runs first, its full SPELL_STATE emit (Cooldowns.lua:339) reaches the old pool, which is released right after. After that, Cooldowns:Refresh only emits on StateChanged (around 455-505), so an interrupt on cooldown can read 'ready' until its state next changes. IconGrid has no pull path from Cooldowns. It cannot be confirmed without the client, but the ordering hazard is real.

findings.title: Every Spells-page edit renders the page twice, and an error mid-render leaves the render guard stuck for the session
findings.evidence: doCommit calls RefreshRows and then FireConfigChanged, whose synchronous subscriber calls RefreshRows again. If fillRows raises, rebuildScheduled stays true and every later RefreshRows returns early. The comment's claim that the flag 'is cleared on EVERY exit' is true of the explicit returns only.
findings.remediation: doCommit should call only FireConfigChanged when the addon is up, and call RefreshRows directly only when NS.IsDown(), because StandDown has unregistered the CONFIG_CHANGED subscriber. Make RefreshRows run its body in a pcall/xpcall (or an equivalent) that always resets rebuildScheduled and then re-raises the error. Tests: one RefreshRows per commitSoon flush, and a later refresh still renders after a forced fillRows raise. Drop slash-commands-§7 as the rule_ref: this is a correctness defect, not a standards deviation.
findings.verify_reason: The finding is real. doCommit (Spells.lua:404-407) calls RefreshRows and then FireConfigChanged. Helpers.FireConfigChanged (Panel.lua:144-156) sends synchronously outside a Coalesced batch, and the subscriber at Spells.lua:1345-1350 calls RefreshRows again, so the page renders twice. The two calls run sequentially, and the flag is cleared at 1243 between them, so the second render really happens. rebuildScheduled is set at 1182 and cleared only on the explicit returns (1189, 1236, 1243), so a raise in fillRows latches it for the session. The impact is small: one extra render of a short spell list per debounced edit, and the stuck flag needs an error in fillRows first. Medium overstates it, so it drops to low. slash-commands-§7 is not what is violated here. It only explains why the direct render must stay while NS.IsDown(): Spells.StandDown at 1422-1429 unregisters the subscriber. That part of the remediation is correct.

findings.title: docs/performance.md's bucket table does not match the Perf descriptor, and spellState runs outside its declared stateEmit parent on the Rebuild path
findings.evidence: performance.md says spellState sits within spellPoll, omits stateEmit, and says glowGate is 'deliberately not declared'. PerfSetup declares stateEmit within spellPoll, spellState within stateEmit, and glowGate. The Rebuild emit at Cooldowns.lua:339 is not bracketed as stateEmit, and Perf.Note('spellState') at IconGrid.lua:994 passes no parent. The committed captures (20260909-014035) predate the current nesting.
findings.remediation: Fix the Rebuild path so the declared nesting is true at every level. Either (a) bracket Rebuild's emit under its own undeclared or root bucket (e.g. 'rebuildEmit', no within) and have IconGrid:OnSpellState pass its observed parent to Perf.Note, so LibKa0s-Perf reports observedMixed honestly, or (b) drop stateEmit's 'within = spellPoll' and state in PerfSetup that stateEmit has two callers. Then regenerate the docs/performance.md bucket table from the PerfSetup descriptor, including stateEmit and glowGate and removing the 'glowGate not declared' paragraph. Add a test_perfsetup case asserting every spellState note happens under an open stateEmit and that stateEmit's observed parent matches its declaration. Re-run tests/perf.lua. The in-game two-arm capture via /wow-addon:perf-analysis stays as the smoke step.
findings.verify_reason: Real. docs/performance.md:36-55 lists spellState within spellPoll, has no stateEmit row, and says glowGate is 'deliberately not declared'. core/PerfSetup.lua:100-101,105 declares stateEmit within spellPoll, spellState within stateEmit, and glowGate. Cooldowns.lua:339 (Rebuild's SendMessage) has no bracket, while the Refresh emits at :452/:505 are bracketed as stateEmit with parent 'spellPoll'. IconGrid.lua:994 notes spellState with no parent. Severity goes down to low. The mis-nesting only happens on the Rebuild path, which runs on spell or spec changes and never per frame. The harm is a misleading nesting line in perf reports, not a runtime defect. The remediation also has a gap. If Rebuild's emit is bracketed as stateEmit with parent nil, stateEmit's own declared parent (within spellPoll) is still false on that path, because Rebuild never runs inside Cooldowns:Refresh. That moves the false claim up one level instead of removing it.

findings.title: The Spells remove button uses the one-off Blizzard atlas transmog-icon-remove instead of a LibKa0s catalog mark
findings.evidence: The catalog carries close, clear and cancel, which NS.Icon resolves. This is a cosmetic drift from the other Ka0s list editors.
findings.remediation: In rowRemoveButton (settings/Spells.lua:797-798), pass image = NS.Icon and NS.Icon('clear') (or 'close'), and keep atlas = 'transmog-icon-remove' only as the fallback when NS.Icon returns nil. The existing opts.image -> SetImage branch handles the path, so no new branch is needed. Put image ahead of atlas in makeRowIconBtn's if-chain. Optionally tint via SetVertexColor, since catalog marks are white-in-alpha. Rewrite the comment at Spells.lua:563-567 so it no longer says the atlas is required. Upstream work (a new 'remove' mark in LibKa0s tools/artwork, then a release and a re-vendor) only if neither clear nor close reads right.
findings.verify_reason: Real. settings/Spells.lua:798 passes atlas = "transmog-icon-remove", and anti-patterns.md #63 names 'a Blizzard atlas where LibKa0s-Media-1.0 carries the mark' explicitly. The catalog (libs/LibKa0s/Media.lua:94-97) has clear, close, cancel and ban. Low severity is right because the problem is cosmetic. The remediation is overbuilt: makeRowIconBtn (Spells.lua:590-600) already has an opts.image branch that calls btn:SetImage(path), and NS.Icon (core/MediaSetup.lua:72) returns an extensionless path, so no new opts.icon/SetTexture branch is needed. The remediation also misses two things. NS.Icon returns nil when the library is absent, so the atlas should stay as the fallback. The builder comment at Spells.lua:563-567, which says the atlas is needed, goes stale and needs updating. This is the only makeRowIconBtn call site.

findings.title: Load-bearing TOC position with no annotation: modules\IconGrid_Layout.lua calls NS:GetModule('IconGrid') at file scope
findings.evidence: Non-silent GetModule raises if IconGrid.lua has not loaded, so the position is load-bearing. This is the root of the four C-16a-d dependents.
findings.remediation: D5/Sprint 3.1: add '# LOAD-BEARING POSITION: the IconGrid_* / Castbar_* siblings call NS:GetModule(<parent>) at file scope, so each follows its parent' above the IconGrid group (:96-97) and the Castbar group (:99-101). Two comments close the root and all four dependents.
findings.verify_reason: KickCD.toc:96 lists modules\IconGrid_Layout.lua with no comment, and modules/IconGrid_Layout.lua:15 calls NS:GetModule("IconGrid") at file scope. toc-file-§5 ('A line whose position is load-bearing MUST carry a comment ... naming what resolves at load') says each load-bearing position is one MUST row. Because the failure is a loud AceAddon load error rather than a silent one, the reachable impact is low, and so is the severity. The siblings do not depend on each other at file scope (grep found no file-scope reads of IconGrid./Castbar. members), so one comment per group that names the parent is accurate. The comment should say it is NS:GetModule("IconGrid") that resolves at load, which meets the 'naming what resolves' requirement.

findings.title: Unclear whether slash-commands-§2's reserved enable/disable verbs reach sub-trees like /kcd spells enable|disable
findings.evidence: §2 says the reserved verbs MUST NOT be reused for anything else, but the standard's own §3 debug example uses enable/disable as sub-arguments. The sub-tree keeps dispatch unambiguous. Not filed as a MUST failure until the standard rules.
findings.remediation: Sprint 0.2: ask WowAddonStandards to rule on whether slash-commands-§2's ban ('enabling a module, a feature or a unit is that thing's own verb or row', slash-commands.md:31) reaches sub-tree verbs, citing the text rather than the §3 debug example. Sprint 5.5: if it does, rename /kcd spells enable|disable to a non-reserved pair such as track/untrack across COMMANDS, help, docs and tests. Otherwise make no change and record the ruling.
findings.verify_reason: core/KickCD.lua:733-736 registers enable/disable under the spells sub-tree to toggle individual spells. The ambiguity is real, but the evidence is off. The §3 debug example (slash-commands.md:62) takes the sub-arguments `on`/`off` and uses 'enable/disable' only in help prose, so it is not precedent for enable/disable as sub-verbs. Also, slash-commands.md:31 leans against KickCD: 'MUST NOT re-use either verb for anything else — enabling a module, a feature or a unit is that thing's own verb or row'. Its stated collision, though, is about the top-level `/<slash> disable`, so a sub-tree is still arguably outside it. Asking the standard for a ruling is right, and info holds until the standard rules.
